==Problem==
Two teams are in a best-two-out-of-three playoff: the teams will play at most <imath>3</imath> games, and the winner of the playoff is the first team to win <imath>2</imath> games. The first game is played on Team A's home field, and the remaining games are played on Team B's home field. Team A has a <imath>\frac{2}{3}</imath> chance of winning at home, and its probability of winning when playing away from home is <imath>p</imath>. Outcomes of the games are independent. The probability that Team A wins the playoff is <imath>\frac{1}{2}</imath>. Then <imath>p</imath> can be written in the form <imath>\frac{1}{2}(m - \sqrt{n})</imath>, where <imath>m</imath> and <imath>n</imath> are positive integers. What is <imath>m + n</imath>?

<imath>\textbf{(A) } 10 \qquad \textbf{(B) } 11 \qquad \textbf{(C) } 12 \qquad \textbf{(D) } 13 \qquad \textbf{(E) } 14</imath>

==Solution==
We only have three cases where A wins: AA, ABA, and BAA (A denotes a team A win and B denotes a team B win). Knowing this, we can sum up the probability of each case. Thus the total probability is <imath>\frac{2}{3}p+\frac{2}{3}(1-p)p+\frac{1}{3}p^2=\frac{1}{2}</imath>. Multiplying  both sides by 6 yields <imath>4p+4p(1-p)+2p^2=3</imath>, so <imath>2p^2-8p+3=0</imath> and we find that <imath>p=\frac{4\pm\sqrt{10}}{2}</imath>. Luckily, we know that the answer should contain  <imath>\frac{1}{2}(m - \sqrt{n})</imath>, so the solution is <imath>p=\frac{4-\sqrt{10}}{2}=\frac{1}{2}(4-\sqrt{10})</imath> and the answer is <imath>4+10=\boxed{\textbf{(E) } 14}</imath>.

~eevee9406

Another way to see the answer is subtraction and not addition is to realize that <imath>p</imath> is between <imath>0</imath> and <imath>1</imath> since it is a probability.
~andliu766
